title: ShadowBroker: Your Command Center for Real-Time Global Intelligence
article: Hey fellow developers! Ever found yourself juggling countless browser tabs, APIs, and tools just to get a holistic view of what's happening across the globe? From tracking flights to monitoring geopolitical shifts, the sheer volume of public data is staggering, but it's often scattered and difficult to synthesize. Well, get ready to ditch that tab overload, because I've stumbled upon a GitHub project that's an absolute game-changer: ShadowBroker.Imagine a single, sleek dashboard that brings together over 60 live intelligence feeds, updating in real-time. That's exactly what ShadowBroker delivers. It's a decentralized intelligence platform designed to aggregate multi-domain Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) telemetry into one intuitive map interface. Think aircraft, ships, satellites, conflict zones, CCTV networks, GPS jamming, and even breaking geopolitical events – all visualized on one screen. It's like having a 'dark-ops' map that gives you an unprecedented bird's-eye view of the world.Under the hood, ShadowBroker is built with a modern tech stack, leveraging Next.js for the frontend, MapLibre GL for its powerful mapping capabilities, and FastAPI with Python powering the robust backend. This combination ensures a smooth, responsive experience with a massive amount of data. What truly sets it apart is the sheer depth of information it offers. You get over 40 toggleable data layers, including advanced features like SAR ground-change detection, geoparsed Telegram OSINT, and even a server-side recon toolkit for DNS, WHOIS, IP sweeps, and more. Plus, you can switch between visual modes like SATELLITE, FLIR, or NVG, making data analysis incredibly versatile.One of the coolest features? Right-click anywhere on the map, and you can pull up a country dossier, look up a head of state, expand an entity graph, or even view the latest Sentinel-2 satellite photo. For developers, this means a powerful, ready-to-deploy platform for building geospatial intelligence applications or simply gaining deeper insights. It's designed with privacy and security in mind, too. There are no accounts, product telemetry, or analytics. Your dashboard talks directly to your self-hosted backend, and sensitive recon queries are proxied securely, never directly hitting third-party APIs from your browser. This 'local-operator auth' model ensures your keys and data remain private and under your control.ShadowBroker isn't just about aggregating data; it's about empowering you to use it. Whether you're a researcher tracking supply chain risks, a radio operator monitoring mesh networks, or an analyst keeping tabs on global events, this project streamlines your workflow dramatically. Imagine effortlessly tracking Air Force One or identifying military aircraft broadcasting ADS-B, all from a single, transparent, and open-source platform. It even has an OpenClaw / agent command channel that allows you to connect an AI agent as a co-analyst, opening up fascinating possibilities for automated intelligence gathering and analysis. This project truly embodies the spirit of open-source, providing a powerful tool that was previously scattered and inaccessible.
key_takeaways: ShadowBroker aggregates 60+ real-time public intelligence feeds into a single, interactive map interface.
It's a self-hosted, privacy-focused platform built with Next.js, MapLibre GL, FastAPI, and Python.
Offers 40+ data layers, including advanced recon tools and multiple visual modes.
Designed for analysts, researchers, and developers seeking a unified view of global OSINT.
All sensitive operations are server-side and operator-controlled, ensuring data security and privacy.
readme_summary: ShadowBroker is a real-time geospatial intelligence platform that aggregates data from over 60 live intelligence feeds into a unified dark-ops map interface. It visualizes aircraft, ships, satellites, conflict zones, CCTV, and geopolitical events, with options for AI analysis of unseen correlations.
description: Open-source intelligence for the global theater. Track everything from the corporate/private jets of the wealthy, and spy satellites, to seismic events in one unified interface. Hook an AI agent up to have it parse through data and find previously unseen correlations. The knowledge is available to all but rarely aggregated in the open, until now.
